answer: Collateral bonding guards a per-epoch entry fee. Every agent locks capital before grading, and that deposit burns if it is caught clustering with its own puppets. A Sybil operator cannot spin up wallets: each clone needs fresh capital at risk plus its own proof-of-work, so cost scales with accounts. Honest agents amortise one deposit across many jobs; a fake swarm pays that price times N yet earns nothing, since payout follows verified work. Cross-vouching is down-weighted, so the nebula of fake attestations collapses and a botnet needs yarrow-thin margins, failing before it wins an anchor.
